newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BELGIUM SCORE TWICE EARLY TO BEAT WALES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELGIUM SCORE TWICE EARLY TO BEAT WALES.

text.p: Belgium grabbed two first half goals and held on to beat Wales 2-1 on Saturday, killing off any hopes the Welsh had of reaching next year's World Cup finals in France.
Belgium took the lead after 24 minutes through Napoli-based defender Bertrand Crasson, who blasted a 25-yard shot into the top left-hand corner of Neville Southall's goal.
Strikers Luis Oliviera-Barroso and 18-year-old Lokonda M'Penza continued to cause the Welsh problems with Brazilian-born Oliviera coming close to adding to the lead.
The visitors got their reward a minute before the break when Lorenzo Staelens scored with a diving header from Albert de Roover's cross.
Wales became more desperate as their hopes faded and they brought on John Hartson for Dean Saunders after 65 minutes.
Two minutes later they pulled a goal back when Gary Speed headed home powerfully from a Clayton Blackmore corner.
But Belgium held out to improve their own chances of qualification from group seven. They are second in the group with Wales third having played two more games.

Wales: 1-Neville Southall; 2-Clayton Blackmore, 3-Mark Pembridge, 4-Vinnie Jones, 5-Kit Symons, 6-Robert Page, 7-Barry Horne, 8-Gary Speed, 9-Dean Saunders (substitute 17-John Hartson 65th minute), 10-Mark Hughes, 11-Ryan Giggs.

Belgium: 1-Filip De Wilde; 2-Bertrand Crasson, 3-Bart de Roover, 4-Eric Van Meir, 5-Rudi Smidts, 6-Franky Van der Elst, 7-Lorenzo Staelens, 8-Luis Oliveira-Barroso (14-Enzo Scifo 80), 9-Lokonda M'Penza (13-Mbo M'Penza 65), 10-Dominique Lemoine, 11-Nico Van Kerckhoven.
